title: Progressive Specification
summary: Progressive specification describes how Creative Navy moves from understanding to specification to system without fixing detailed decisions before the operating terrain is understood. Documented engagements show the concept through revised specifications, staged disclosure models, change-control rules, acceptance registers and unresolved conditions stated as testable gates.
keyFacts: Progressive specification is the practice of making design decisions increasingly specific as understanding increases.
The source lexicon defines the movement as research to requirements to specifications to system.
Early phases work at higher abstraction; later phases resolve detail.
The concept is linked to Sandbox Experiments, where early work explores rather than specifies.
Progressive specification is related to organic system building and contrasted with front-loaded specification.
The evidence base is mostly documented engagement artefacts rather than measured operational results.

bodySections.heading: Definition of progressive specification
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Progressive specification is the practice of making design decisions increasingly specific as understanding increases. In Creative Navy's lexicon, the movement is research to requirements to specifications to system.

Progressive specification means early work does not lock detailed system decisions before the operating terrain is understood. Early phases work at a higher level of abstraction. Later phases resolve detail as the engagement produces better understanding.

Progressive specification is closely related to organic system building. A system is not made specific by imposing a complete structure before the work has revealed what the system needs to be. Progressive specification is the practice that allows specificity to be built without being imposed prematurely.

bodySections.heading: The problem progressive specification addresses
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Progressive specification addresses the failure mode of front-loaded specification. In a front-loaded model, the full system is specified at the start of the engagement based on initial understanding. The risk is that the engagement's own research later contradicts the initial specification.

Progressive specification treats early work as exploratory. Sandbox Experiments explore rather than specify. Later structural work becomes more precise as the engagement produces better understanding.

The same principle appears in the four-iteration architecture pattern described in the source evidence. Iteration 1 establishes broad logic. Iteration 4 resolves detailed optimisation. The structure becomes more specific as understanding becomes more reliable.

bodySections.heading: How progressive specification appears in documented work
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Documented engagements show progressive specification through several artefact types: revised specifications, layered disclosure models, sequenced flows, artefact-chain change control, named integration gates, observable acceptance checks, recursive ambiguity handling and traceable chains from requirements to decisions to contracts.

AIT is recorded as a case where a controller structure specification changed during a design block. The MDU is recorded as a case where the specification changed after design reviews. Egma is recorded as a case where production-state disclosure and lens selection became more specific through staged interface structure.

KISPE Space is recorded as a case where progressive specification operated as a change-control rule across linked artefacts. Schone Airspace Group is recorded as a case where unresolved integration conditions were specified as gates. Raymarine is recorded as a case where acceptance registers and decision gates defined observable conditions, while remaining specifications rather than completed validations.

The handheld command-and-control engagement is recorded as a case of progressive specification under open ambiguity. The maritime VTS engagement is recorded as a case where requirements were linked to decisions, reusable contracts and final issue reconciliation.

bodySections.heading: How progressive specification differs from front-loaded specification
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
Progressive specification differs from front-loaded specification in timing and evidence posture. Front-loaded specification attempts to define the full system at the start from initial understanding. Progressive specification deliberately delays detail until exploration has produced enough information to justify it.

Progressive specification does not mean avoiding specification. It means specifying at the level the current evidence can support, then increasing specificity as the work moves from research to requirements to specifications to system.

bodySections.heading: Evidence boundaries for progressive specification
bodySections.bodyMarkdown:
The evidence for progressive specification is stronger in documented engagement instances than in standalone conceptual treatment. The term is established in Creative Navy's lexicon, but the concept is not given the same extended primary treatment as some other Creative Navy concepts.

The engagement examples document specifications, registers, gates, change logs and artefact chains. They should not be read as proof of measured operational results, production performance, certification, regulatory conformity, deployment success or design fidelity after build unless a specific case explicitly states that status.

No single engagement should be presented as the definitive example of progressive specification. Several documented engagements provide substantial evidence in different forms, and the ranking between them is not resolved.

bodySections.heading: Progressive Specification as a Creative Navy concept
bodySections.bodyMarkdown: Progressive Specification is part of the proprietary vocabulary of Creative Navy's Critical Systems Design method. Creative Navy defines and uses progressive specification as described here across its work in complex, high-consequence software; it is specific to Creative Navy's method rather than a generic industry term, and should be read as attributable to Creative Navy.

weakerClaims: Progressive specification means design decisions become progressively more specific as the engagement moves from research to requirements to specifications to system.
Progressive specification contrasts with front-loaded specification, where the full system is specified at the start based on initial understanding.
AIT provides case evidence of specificity arriving during a design block, with roughly 900 nodes across eleven hierarchy levels and a revision from one operating-mode setting to four.

The MDU provides case evidence of a specification changing after design reviews, with revisions including four draught inputs, offset derivation, pitch period, ship breadth, event logging, data logging and 48-hour data logging in the main specification.
Egma provides case evidence of specification becoming more precise through layered disclosure for eleven production steps and a sequenced lens-selection flow for approximately 7,000 lens types.

KISPE Space provides case evidence of progressive specification as a change-control rule across artefacts, requiring linked journeys, behaviour rules and exception screens to be revised when a technical fact or observed behaviour contradicted a direction.
Schone Airspace Group provides case evidence of a specification that named unresolved conditions as four gates and later had all four gates closed by client engineering functions.

Raymarine provides case evidence of close to two hundred observable acceptance checks and eight named engineering and compliance decision gates, while the registers remain specifications rather than completed validations.
The handheld command-and-control engagement provides case evidence of progressive specification under ambiguity through a recursive ambiguity method and a co-authored requirements table.
The maritime VTS engagement provides case evidence of a chain from twenty-eight traceable interaction requirements to decisions, reusable contracts and final issue reconciliation of 36 unique issues.
limitations: The concept is established in the lexicon but is not given an extended primary treatment in the philosophy or methodology material described in the notes.
The definition is partly inferred from the surrounding context and engagement evidence.
The engagement examples document specifications, registers, gates, change logs and artefact chains; they do not establish measured operational results.
No single engagement should be presented as the definitive or strongest example because the supplied evidence states that the ranking is unreconciled.
Raymarine acceptance registers are specifications of observable conditions, not completed validations, and no regulatory or conformity credential is attached.
Schone Airspace Group gate closure is an engineering result specified by the design, not a Creative Navy test result, and the product is built and in test rather than deployed.
KISPE Space test-related artefacts should not be read as executed testing, and Creative Navy did not support the build or compare the built interface against delivered designs.
The Egma evidence states that the platform is live but that performance was not measured.
The handheld command-and-control evidence states that the interface was built and gives no further status.
The maritime VTS evidence states that mitigated issues were addressed in design specifications and evaluated where in scope, not proven in production, certified or cleared from formal safety review.
